record.original_question: Does there exist a planar graph G whose list packing number chi*_l(G) is at least 6?

evidence.quote: The list packing number chi*_l(G) of G is the least k such that G admits an L-packing of size k for any k-list-assignment L of G.
Problem 2.6 Is there a planar graph with chi*_l(G) >= 6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for G is a function L that assigns to each vertex v of G a finite set L(v) of colors; if |L(v)| = k for every vertex v, we call L a k-list-assignment. An L-coloring of G is a proper coloring f of G such that f(v) ∈ L(v) for every vertex v. For a list assignment L of G, an L-packing of size k is a collection (f_1, ..., f_k) of L-colorings of G that are pairwise disjoint, meaning that for every vertex v the colors f_1(v), ..., f_k(v) are all distinct (in particular, k ≤ |L(v)| for every v). The list packing number χ*_ℓ(G) is the least integer k such that, for every k-list-assignment L of G, the graph G admits an L-packing of size k.

Question: Does there exist a planar graph G (i.e., a graph that can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings) with χ*_ℓ(G) ≥ 6?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Cranston and Smith-Roberge (2024) establishes upper bounds χ*_ℓ(G) ≤ 8 for planar graphs, ≤ 5 for planar graphs of girth ≥ 4, and ≤ 4 for girth ≥ 5, but constructions only achieve χ*_ℓ(G) = 4 (e.g. for outerplanar graphs). Whether any planar graph attains χ*_ℓ(G) ≥ 6 remains open.

status_evidence.title: List Packing and Correspondence Packing of Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: For planar graphs χ*_ℓ(G) ≤ 8; for girth ≥ 4, ≤ 5; for girth ≥ 5, ≤ 4. Outerplanar constructions reach χ*_ℓ = 4.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds are known but no planar graph with χ*_ℓ ≥ 6 has been constructed; the question remains open.
